turns.text: When my commute became much longer, I started listening to podcasts. At Johnson Space Center, NASA had mostly highlight shows, short recaps with audio from video.
They were more like shows just put in audio.
I thought we should make a real podcast. I researched the industry and audience, then presented statistics to management and argued NASA should enter that space.
We had to explain what a podcast was to a lot of people.
That was a big part of it. We needed to build it from scratch and create weekly content that could go out through NASA.gov.
Then came the fun part: what were we going to call it, and what would it look like?
Kelly Humphreys came up with Houston, We Have a Podcast.
That name was natural and memorable. It was the one that fit.
That's the one. It was too perfect.
